item.content:encoded: Bit of authorial headcanon on 2245: The Collective is still somewhat nebulous, probably something of a non-profit, but one of their consistent features is the delivery of dreams. item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm conflicted on this tale. On the one hand, I enjoy the interpretation, behaviour, and presented origin of the Oneiroi. I think the contrast between their view of the end of their civilization and the Foundation's provided an interesting narrative.

On the other hand, the interpretation of SCP-990 felt like providing a relatively mundane, unsatisfying answer to what was originally a quite entertaining mystery. It didn't help that this tale often found ways to jettison elements of 990 (the appearance, the high-numbered SCP) rather than incorporate them. For example, the change in the iconic appearance mostly came across as an excuse to use a different cool picture.

Given the deliberate pinning down of the mystery, the reversion to a state of uncertainty at the end felt a little cheap.

I still enjoyed certain elements of that narrative, including the multiversal Foundation callously experimenting with human extinction and the potential categorization of the operative as anomalous. Even with that, I can't help but see this interpretation as a downgrade to the original. No vote.

The interpretation of the Oneiroi Collective as a business entity is based on several other articles on said GoI.

I will see them as largely neutral (they won't care what people do with their products), just want proper recognition and credit when it's due. I will say that money is a lesser concern; it is the thought that counts.

I don't mind them being bad (or even just not-good) but it's hard to believe a group exisiting in dreams and operating on surreal and weightless logic… is a company trying to make money. It was close to bringing the article down for me, and while I think this interpretation of them is fine, I can't say I'm for it.

item.title: Thanks, Attribution and Other Matters
item.content:encoded:
Firstly, thanks to reviewers such as augmentedspartan and psul.

Secondly, the image used is from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immersion_(virtual_reality)#/media/File:AC89-0437-20_a.jpegunder) under Public Domain.

SCPs featured include: SCP-990 (Dream Man) by Dave Rapp

Thirdly, this Tale is part of the "series" that is in canon with How 173 Got to Site-19. The Foundation on the mutliversal scale, as a literal foundation over all realities. This also doubles as a re-imagining of SCP-990 and the Oneiroi Collective.
